Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ), which is expressed in a variety of malignancies, governs biological functions through transcriptional programs. Defining the molecular mechanisms governing the selection of canonical versus non-canonical PPARγ binding sequences may provide the opportunity to design regulators with distinct functions and side effects. Acetylation at K268/293 in mouse Pparγ2 participates in the regulation of adipose tissue differentiation, and the conserved lysine residues (K154/155) in mouse Pparγ1 governs lipogenesis in breast cancer cells. Herein, the PPARγ1 acetylated residues K154/155 were shown to be essential for oncogenic ErbB2 driven breast cancer growth and mammary tumor stem cell expansion in vivo. The induction of transcriptional modules governing growth factor signaling, lipogenesis, cellular apoptosis, and stem cell expansion were dependent upon K154/155. The acetylation status of the K154/155 residues determined the selection of genome-wide DNA binding sites, altering the selection from canonical to non-canonical (C/EBP) DNA sequence-specific binding. The gene signature reflecting the acetylation-dependent genomic occupancy in lipogenesis provided predictive value in survival outcomes of ErbB2 + breast cancer. The Pparγ1 acetylation site is critical for ErbB2-induced breast cancer tumor growth and may represent a relevant target for therapeutic coextinction. extracted_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated the role of PPARγ1, specifically its K154/155 acetylation site, as a molecular switch in oncogenic ErbB2- and Ha-Ras-driven mammary adenocarcinoma tumor growth, stem cell expansion, and metastasis. Using in vitro cell models, in vivo mouse xenograft models, and human breast cancer patient datasets, the research demonstrated that K154/155 acetylation is essential for promoting tumor growth, de novo lipogenesis, and cancer stem cell characteristics, while also regulating cellular apoptosis and autophagy. The acetylation status was found to determine genome-wide DNA binding site selection, shifting from canonical to non-canonical (C/EBP) binding, and influencing transcriptional programs for growth factor signaling. Furthermore, gene signatures reflecting acetylation-dependent genomic occupancy in lipogenesis (PASS1 and PASS2) showed predictive value for survival outcomes and distant metastasis-free survival in various breast cancer subtypes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Molecular mechanism investigation focusing on PPARγ1 post-translational modification (acetylation) and the functional consequences of genetic variants (wild-type vs. acetylation-defective mutants)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily involved comparing wild-type PPARγ1 with specific genetic variants (acetylation-defective mutants K154/155Q, K154/155A, an acetylation mimic K154/155R, and a sumoylation site mutant K77R) expressed in various breast cancer cell lines (MCF10A-NeuT, MCF10A-Ha-Ras, MCF10A-Src) and in vivo in mouse xenograft models and transgenic mice with inducible Pparγ1 deletion. Experiments often involved subcutaneous injection of 1 x 10^6 cells. No dose-response comparisons of external therapeutic agents were reported; the focus was on the impact of specific molecular modifications and genetic manipulations, with the K154/155Q mutant demonstrating a significant ~90% reduction in tumor growth.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Mammary adenocarcinoma tumors, breast cancer cells (MCF10A-NeuT, MCF10A-Ha-Ras, MCF10A-Src), mammary epithelial cells, human breast cancer samples (breast epithelium), and chromatin
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Protein acetylation level, protein binding (ChIP-Seq, ChIP-qPCR), gene expression (mRNA), nuclear receptor function influencing DNA binding and gene transcription, molecular switch

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Acetylation at K154/155 promotes tumor growth; K154/155 mutation reduces acetylation and overall chromatin binding, and alters DNA binding specificity. PPARG mRNA abundance increased in breast cancer patients compared to healthy women, but also reported as reduced in breast cancer (need to clarify if it refers to total protein/mRNA vs. active form)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Acetylation at K154/155 was essential for oncogenic ErbB2-driven breast cancer growth and mammary tumor stem cell expansion, inducing transcriptional modules for growth factor signaling, lipogenesis, apoptosis, and stem cell expansion. The K154/155 mutation significantly reduced [3H] acetyl-CoA incorporation and total PPARγ1 chromatin binding from 25,174 sites (WT) to 2849 sites. Acetylation also governs PPARγ-mediated tumor growth, stem cell expansion, and autophagy by augmenting non-canonical C/EBP binding. Relative abundance of PPARG was increased in breast cancer patients (Fig. S18B) and inversely correlated with SIRT1 (r = -0.13, p = 1.875E-009). Conversely, a reduction in PPARG mRNA in breast cancer was also noted (Fig. S18A).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Nuclear receptor that governs biological functions through transcriptional programs; determines selection of genome-wide DNA binding sites (canonical vs. non-canonical C/EBP sites); regulates growth factor signaling, lipid biogenesis, cellular apoptosis, autophagy, differentiation, inflammation, insulin sensitivity, cellular proliferation, and stem cell expansion. Serves as a molecular switch for breast tumor growth.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Oncogenic ErbB2- and Ha-Ras-driven mammary tumorigenesis, breast cancer onset and progression, human breast cancer patient analysis, and post-translational modification in breast cancer cell models and xenografts.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Critical for ErbB2-induced breast cancer tumor growth and mammary epithelial stem cell initiation/self-renewal; may represent a relevant therapeutic target. Its acetylation site-mediated transcriptional output is crucial for tumor growth, lipogenesis, and anti-apoptotic functions. A significant reduction in binding sites for the K154/155Q mutant indicates substantial alteration in gene expression regulation, contributing to its altered functions and suggesting prognostic significance in human breast cancer.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Cell Proliferation Markers (Cell Proliferation Rate, S phase enrichment, Cyclin D1, Tumor Growth)
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: MCF10A-NeuT cells, mammary fat pad of nude mice (xenograft tumors), tumor tissues (MCF10A-NeuT)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Cellular growth assay, cell cycle phase analysis, protein level, tumor volume/size measurement

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher with PPARγ1 WT and K77R mutant; lower with K154/155Q mutant. Cyclin D1 showed a trend towards reduction with K154/155Q mutant
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: PPARγ1 WT and K77R mutant increased cell proliferation and S phase enrichment. K154/155Q mutant failed to induce proliferation and reduced S phase enrichment by ~90%. PPARγ1 WT promoted MCF10A-NeuT tumor growth in mice, with K154/155Q reducing growth-enhancing function (P = 0.00011) and K77R increasing growth (P = 0.0099). PPARγ1 K154/155Q reduced MCF10A-Ha-Ras tumor growth by 75%. Cyclin D1 showed a trend toward reduction in K154/155Q compared to WT.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Regulation of cell cycle progression, DNA synthesis, and neoplastic cell mass increase
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Transfection of PPARγ1 variants into MCF10A cells and xenograft models of mammary tumorigenesis
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Direct indicators of tumor development and growth, showing that PPARγ1 K154/155 acetylation promotes proliferation and tumor growth.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Lipid Metabolism Markers (Lipid Production, Intracellular Triglyceride Concentration, SCD1, FASN, SREBP1, SREBP2, FABP4, SCD, SREBF2, ADIPOQ, de novo breast tumor lipogenesis)
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: MCF10A-NeuT cells, MCF10A-NeuT xenograft tumor samples, promoters of genes
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Staining intensity, concentration measurement, protein level (Western blot, IHC), transcription factor level, gene regulatory region binding, cellular metabolic process

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher with PPARγ1 WT, K154/155R, K77R; lower with K154/155Q, K154/155A. PPARγ1 K154/155Q mutant abrogated/reduced lipogenesis, and reduced expression/abundance/binding of SCD1, FASN, SREBP1, SREBP2, FABP4, SCD, SREBF2, ADIPOQ. SREBP1 and SREBP2 are induced by PPARγ1 via K154/155 site
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 3- to 4-fold induction of Oil-Red O staining with WT/K154/155R/K77R, ~90% reduction with K154/155Q/K154/155A. Intracellular triglycerides increased in WT vs K154/155Q (2.31 ± 0.11 vs 0.42 ± 0.06 nmol/5000 cells, p < 0.001). SCD1, FASN, SREBP1, SREBP2 protein levels reduced in K154/155Q mutant tumors. K154/155Q mutant tumors demonstrated less robust lipogenesis. Reduced binding of PPARγ1 K154/155Q compared with WT at regulatory regions of FABP4, SCD, SREBF2, ADIPOQ. SREBP1/2 were previously shown to correlate with poor prognosis in breast cancer.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Lipid synthesis and storage (lipogenesis), cellular lipid metabolism and energy storage, fatty acid synthesis, transcription factors for lipogenesis
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Genetic manipulation of PPARγ1 variants in MCF10A-NeuT cells and mammary tumorigenesis in xenograft models. Regulation of lipid biogenesis in breast tumor xenografts dependent on PPARγ1 K154/155 acetylation
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the role of PPARγ1 acetylation in regulating cellular lipid production and de novo lipogenesis, which is essential for rapid tumor cell proliferation. Reduced lipogenesis suggests inhibited tumor growth. SREBP1/2 induction correlates with poor prognosis.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Apoptosis Markers (Cell Death, Active caspase-3, Bcl-XL, Apoptosis-promoting Genes)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Histological staining, protein level (IHC, Western blot), gene transcript level

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Increased cell death and active caspase-3 with PPARγ1 K154/155Q mutant. Decreased Bcl-XL with K154/155Q mutant. Apoptosis-promoting genes (PRMT1, EP300, PYCARD, TP63) higher with K154/155Q mutant
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased TUNEL staining and active caspase-3 in K154/155Q mutant tumors. Bcl-XL abundance reduced by ~90% (N=6) in K154/155Q mutant tumors.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Programmed cell death, tumor suppression. Bcl-XL is an anti-apoptotic protein
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Mammary tumorigenesis with PPARγ1 K154/155Q mutant expression
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased apoptosis and reduced anti-apoptotic signaling (Bcl-XL) in K154/155Q mutant tumors indicate a tumor suppressive effect and improved anti-cancer activity.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Autophagy/Mitophagy Markers (Beclin1, BNIP3L, LC3A II, BNIP3, ATG10)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Protein level (Western blot), gene regulatory region binding

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower in K154/155Q mutant tumors compared to WT
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduced Beclin1, BNIP3L, LC3A II, and BNIP3 in K154/155Q mutant tumors. Enhanced binding of PPARγ1 WT to regulatory regions of autophagy-related genes Bnip3L and ATG10 occurred in an acetylation site-dependent manner (implying reduced binding for K154/155Q mutant).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cellular processes of self-degradation and recycling (autophagy) and selective degradation of mitochondria (mitophagy), involved in cellular homeostasis, stress response, and cancer progression
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Mammary tumorigenesis with PPARγ1 K154/155Q mutant expression and PPARγ1 acetylation site-dependent regulation
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Restraint of autophagy/mitophagy in K154/155Q expressing tumors indicates altered cellular metabolism, potentially hindering tumor cell survival and growth.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Tumor tissues (MCF10A-NeuT), breast tumor xenografts, breast cancer cells/tumors (implied)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Signaling pathway activation (Western blot), protein level, protein phosphorylation, gene expression (induction), protein binding (PPARγ1)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher for ERK, AKT, β-catenin, GSK3 p in PPARγ1 K154/155Q mutant tumors. IL6 induced by PPARγ1 WT, lower in K154/155Q mutant context
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Activation of ERK, AKT, β-catenin, and GSK3 p associated with the PPARγ1 K154/155Q mutant. PPARγ1 WT tumors showed reduced ERK and AKT signaling compared to K154/155Q mutant tumors (implying K154/155Q causes higher activation). IL-6 induced 2-3 fold by PPARγ1 WT, preferentially bound by PPARγ1 WT in ChIP-Seq. IL-6 mRNA was induced 2.6-fold in PPARγ1 WT compared with PPARγ1 K154/155Q.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Regulates cell proliferation, differentiation, survival, and growth (ERK, AKT, Wnt signaling). Cytokine involved in inflammation, linked to cancer stem cell expansion and HER2 inhibition resistance (IL-6)
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Mammary tumorigenesis with PPARγ1 K154/155Q mutant expression, specifically as counter-regulatory survival pathways following apoptosis induction and autophagy restraint. PPARγ1 WT vs K154/155Q mutant affecting IL-6 promoter binding and mRNA induction related to breast cancer stem cell expansion
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher ERK/AKT/Wnt signaling in K154/155Q mutant tumors suggests activation of counter-regulatory survival pathways in response to tumor suppressive effects. Reduced IL-6 in the K154/155Q mutant impedes breast cancer stem cell expansion, potentially improving therapeutic response.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: DNA Binding Specificity (PPARE, RXR, C/EBP, CEBPB, AP-1 motif occupancy)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: DNA binding specificity (TF motif enrichment), transcription factor binding enrichment, protein-DNA binding

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower for PPARE and RXR motifs with K154/155Q mutant; higher for C/EBP motif and CEBPB binding sites with K154/155Q mutant; unchanged for AP-1 binding sites
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: K154/155Q mutant showed ~14% PPARE and ~15.78% RXR motif occupancy in its unique binding peaks, compared to ~32% for WT in its unique peaks. K154/155Q mutant alone binding peaks more frequently overlapped the C/EBP motif (32.48%) than PPARγ1 WT alone (21.88%). CEBPB binding sites were significantly more enriched at K154/155Q mutant only peaks. AP-1 binding sites were not significantly altered.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Regulation of gene expression through specific DNA sequence binding; determines transcriptional targets. C/EBP proteins function as growth inhibitors in breast tissue
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Acetylation of PPARγ1 K154/155 determines DNA binding sequence preference in chromatin in breast cancer cells
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: The K154/155Q mutation significantly alters PPARγ1's DNA binding profile, shifting from canonical (PPARE/RXR) to non-canonical (C/EBP) sites, suggesting altered gene regulation and a potential mechanism for reduced tumor growth (C/EBPs are growth inhibitors).

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: PPARγ1 binding locations (chromatin), FABP, AdipoQ, ATG10, and BNIP3L promoter regions

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Increased H3K9Ac and CBP recruitment with PPARγ1 WT; reduced with K154/155Q mutant
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: H3K9Ac increased at PPARγ1 binding locations in PPARγ1 WT compared with vector control or K154/155Q mutant. CBP was recruited with PPARγ1 WT to promoter regions (e.g., FABP, AdipoQ, ATG10, BNIP3L), but recruitment was reduced with K154/155Q mutant.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: H3K9Ac is enriched at active promoters, indicating active gene transcription. CBP is a PPARγ1 coactivator
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Transcriptional functionality of genome-wide PPARγ binding and co-recruitment with PPARγ1 to promoter regions
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates that K154/155 acetylation is crucial for PPARγ1's transcriptional activity and coactivator recruitment, linking it to active gene expression and tumor-promoting pathways.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Cancer Stem Cell Markers (CD24-/CD44+ Cell Abundance, Mammosphere formation, 'stem cell like' gene expression)
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Mammary epithelial cells (from transgenic mice or MCF10A-NeuT/Ras/Src cells), MCF10A-NeuT cells, breast tumors (PPARγ1 K154/155 mutant tumors, human breast cancer cells expressing oncogenic ErbB2)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Flow cytometry (cell sorting), mammosphere formation assay (count/size), gene expression level, cellular differentiation/proliferation capacity, GSEA

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower with Pparγ1 deficient/K154/155Q mutant; higher with PPARγ1 WT
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Pparγ1 deficient mammary epithelial cells showed a ~3-fold reduction in mammosphere number (p = 0.0011). Mammosphere number/size reduced in MCF10A-NeuT-PPARγ1 K154/155Q, and induced by PPARγ1 WT in MCF10A-Ras and MCF10A-Src lines. GFP+/RFP+ ratio showed a 4.4-fold relative reduction of GFP+ cells in Pparγ1 deficient CK8+ epithelial cells. CD24- CD44+ abundance was enriched in PPARγ1 WT vs K154/155Q. K154/155 mutant tumors conveyed reduced 'stem cell like' gene expression by GSEA.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicators of stem cell characteristics in cancer, associated with tumor initiation, progression, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance; stem cell self-renewal and clonogenic potential
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Genetic deletion of Pparγ1, and expression of PPARγ1 K154/155 acetylation-defective mutant in mammary tumors or human breast cancer cells expressing oncogenic ErbB2
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: PPARγ1, particularly its K154/155 acetylation, is essential for mammary epithelial stem cell initiation/self-renewal. Reduced stem cell characteristics in the K154/155Q mutant are associated with decreased tumor initiation, growth, and potentially improved therapeutic outcomes.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Gene Expression Signatures (PASS1, PASS2, ACSL1, ARID5B, C1QTNF1, IDO1, IQGAP2, PPFIBP2, RGS2, SERTAD4, SLC16A4)
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Human breast cancer patient clinical datasets (microarray), MCF10A-NeuT cell tumors

measured_effect.direction_of_change: PASS1 and PASS2 associated with worse outcomes/shorter survival. The set of other genes (ACSL1, etc.) regulated by K154/155Q mutant contribute to cancer cell demise
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: PASS1 significantly associated with worse outcomes and shorter distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) in all breast cancer patients (p = 0.04) and ERα-negative breast cancer patients (p = 0.007). High PASS1 associated with shorter overall-free survival (OS) in luminal B subtype. PASS2 significantly associated with ERα-negative breast cancer patients, and high expression with poor OS in Her2-positive and basal subtypes. Relative levels of other genes shown in heat map (Fig. S17).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Gene expression modules and lipid metabolism signatures mediated by PPARγ1 K154/155 acetylation, potentially contributing to cancer cell demise
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Clinical analysis of breast cancer patients (all, ERα-negative, luminal B, Her2-positive, basal subtypes) and regulation by PPARγ1 K154/155Q mutant in MCF10A-NeuT cell tumors
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Prognostic markers for worse outcomes and shorter survival in various breast cancer subtypes. Indicates specific gene regulation by K154/155Q mutant that may contribute to anti-cancer effects.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Breast epithelium of healthy women and breast cancer samples

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Reduced in breast cancer; inversely correlated with PPARG abundance
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Reduction in breast cancer (Fig. S18A). Inversely correlated with PPARG (r = -0.13, p = 1.875E-009).

analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Breast cancer context, comparison with healthy women
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduced in breast cancer and inverse correlation with PPARG are relevant to PPARγ regulation and breast cancer prognosis, implying potential therapeutic target.
